**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Tomato stem (close-up, center of frame)
- **Key features**: White, powdery/crusty deposits scattered along the stem surface, overlaid on the normal trichomes (hairs) of the tomato stem
- **Leaves**: Appear green and relatively healthy in background
- **Texture**: The white coating has a dusty/powdery character, not fuzzy/gray, not dark lesions

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery fungal mycelium coating on plant surfaces (stems, leaves) — matches the white powdery deposit visible along the stem
- **Gray Mold** (Botrytis): Gray-brown fuzzy sporulation — not white/powdery, doesn't match
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt**: Dark cankers, vascular browning, bird's eye lesions on fruit — not matching
- **Bacterial_Speck**: Small dark spots on leaves/fruit — not matching stem powder deposits
- **Late_Blight / Early_Blight**: Dark lesions with rings on leaves — not matching
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Circular leaf spots — not matching

The white powdery coating on the tomato stem is the hallmark symptom of **Powdery Mildew** (caused by *Leveillula taurica* or *Oidium neolycopersici* on tomato), which can colonize stems as well as leaves with visible white mycelium.
